transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because of work, honestly. We got this new operations manager recently, and he's just... he's been picking apart the inspection procedures I've used for years. And I mean *years*. I've been sorting and testing on that line since before they even paved the south parking lot. You know, back when Dave was still running the floor. Dave was great, he always brought donuts on Fridays from that little bakery on 4th street—oh, they closed down a while back, which is such a shame because their apple fritters were just out of this world. My husband and I used to go there every weekend. 

Anyway, speaking of my husband, I've been snapping at him a lot lately. I just can't seem to leave work at work anymore. I come home all wound up, and then I'm lying awake at night just replaying these meetings with the new manager over and over in my head. I tried drinking chamomile tea for it because my sister swears by it, but she buys the loose leaf kind and I don't have one of those little metal strainer things. She's always been a bit fancy like that, she moved out to Connecticut last year. 

But um, yeah, because of all this, the next day at work I end up second-guessing routine quality calls that I used to make without any trouble at all. I just don't feel like myself.
Do you find yourself repeatedly thinking about these meetings with the new manager even when you're not trying to?

I'm not really sure if it's like I'm not *trying* to think about it... I haven't really noticed it happening quite like that. I just know I lay there at night and mull over what he said. 

But it really doesn't help that he always schedules these reviews in Conference Room B. That room is just freezing. I swear they keep the air conditioning on full blast year-round, even now in October. I actually had to start bringing my thick wool cardigan to work—the one my niece knitted for me. She's so talented, she just opened an Etsy shop selling these beautiful chunky knit blankets. I bought a sage green one for our guest room because the bed in there is right by a drafty window, and you know how these older houses get. We really need to get those windows resealed before winter hits, but my husband keeps putting it off to watch football on the weekends... 

But um, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the thoughts. Yeah, I don't know if they just pop up out of nowhere against my will, I just know I end up dwelling on them a lot.
Have you been avoiding certain tasks or situations at work since the new manager started?

Well, I haven't really been avoiding the work itself, but... I guess I have been pulling back from some things. Like, I've missed a few internal deadlines lately, which is just not like me at all. My work record has definitely taken a hit. And those meetings I'm supposed to go to? I've been finding excuses to skip them. I just can't sit in that freezing conference room and listen to him talk about "optimizing workflows." 

Speaking of workflows, my husband tried to "optimize" how we load the dishwasher last week. He read some article online about water flow and plate placement, and now he insists all the bowls have to go on the bottom rack. But they don't fit right! The prongs are too close together. I bought this beautiful set of ceramic bowls from a pottery fair in Asheville—we went there for our 25th anniversary, such a lovely trip. The leaves were just starting to turn, and we stayed in this cozy little cabin that smelled like pine... 

But anyway, because of all this stress, we've been arguing a lot more, especially about silly things like the dishwasher. I'm just so drained when I get home that I haven't been keeping up with our usual evening routines. I used to make a nice dinner, maybe do a little gardening out back, but now I just kind of collapse on the sofa. The weeds in my tomato patch are getting completely out of hand. I really need to get out there with the trowel, but I just can't find the energy.
Do you feel like you have to think about these meetings with the new manager, like you can't stop even if you want to?

Well, I wouldn't say I *have* to think about them, like I'm being forced to or anything. It's not like a broken record that I can't turn off. It's just... I get home, and I sit down, and my mind just wanders right back to what he said about my sampling logs. 

Which reminds me, I actually need to buy a new logbook. The ones they supply us at work have this really thin paper, and my pens always bleed through. I like to use those gel pens, you know? The Pilot G2s. I've been using the blue ones for years, but last week I bought a pack of the purple ones just to spice things up. My granddaughter loves purple. She just turned seven, and her whole birthday party was unicorn themed. Purple balloons, purple frosting on the cupcakes... oh, those cupcakes were so sweet they made my teeth ache. I think my daughter got them from that big supermarket chain, not a real bakery. You can always tell the difference in the buttercream. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, the meetings. Yeah, no, I don't feel like I *can't* stop thinking about them if I really tried, I just... I don't know, I just end up dwelling on them when I'm tired.
Are there any specific work tasks or situations that you've been avoiding since the new manager started?

I think we just talked about that, didn't we? I really don't think there's anything else specific, other than what I already mentioned about finding excuses to skip those meetings. I still do my regular sampling and testing on the floor, I haven't been avoiding that. 

It's just those sit-downs with him... I really can't stand being in that room. And it's not just the cold I told you about, it's those horrible mesh chairs they bought for the office last year. They offer absolutely zero lumbar support. My lower back has been acting up so much lately because of them, I actually made my husband go mattress shopping with me this past weekend. We went to that big warehouse store out on Route 9, and let me tell you, the salesmen there are like vultures. They swoop right down on you the second you walk through the automatic doors. We did end up buying a memory foam one, but the delivery guys tracked mud all over my front hallway rug. It's a vintage runner I got from an estate sale, gorgeous red and navy pattern... I spent three hours trying to scrub the stains out with club soda and baking soda. My neighbor Brenda swears by that combination for everything, even her dog's messes. She has a Golden Retriever that just sheds everywhere, sweet dog, but oh, the vacuuming she must have to do... 

Wait, I'm sorry, did you mean a different kind of task? Because yeah, no, nothing specific other than what I said before.
Do you ever have thoughts about the new manager or work situations that feel like they are popping into your head without you wanting them to?

Well, no, not really. They don't just pop in out of the blue like that. It's not like a sudden interruption or anything. 

Speaking of sudden interruptions, though, my cell phone has been ringing off the hook lately with those awful spam calls. Do you get those? It's always some robotic voice telling me my car warranty is about to expire. I drive a 2015 Subaru, I'm pretty sure that ship has sailed! My husband keeps telling me to just ignore numbers I don't recognize, but I always worry it might be the vet calling. Our cat, Barnaby, has been having this awful hairball issue lately. We even switched him to that expensive grain-free food, the salmon pate—he absolutely refuses to eat the chicken one, he'll just sit by his bowl and glare at you until you open a different can. Cats have such attitudes, don't they? He actually knocked over one of my spider plants on the porch yesterday just because he was mad his breakfast was ten minutes late. Dirt went absolutely everywhere.

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right, the thoughts about work. No, they don't force their way in or pop up when I'm doing something else. Like I said before, I just kind of end up dwelling on the manager when I'm already sitting down and feeling tired at the end of the day.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about work when you're trying to focus on something else?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm trying to focus on something else and then work just barges in. It's more like... if I'm watching TV, maybe I'm not really paying attention to the show anyway, you know? 

Like last night, I had one of those home renovation shows on. I used to love those, but lately they all seem exactly the same. Every single house gets open-concept living, gray laminate floors, and a giant kitchen island. Who needs an island that big? You'd have to shout to talk to someone on the other side of it. My husband and I remodeled our kitchen back in 2008, right before the market crashed, and we kept the walls up. I like having the kitchen separate. That way, if I have guests over and the sink is full of dirty pots, nobody has to look at it while we're eating. We did put in granite countertops, though. "Giallo Ornamental," they called it. It has these lovely little flecks of gold and brown. But let me tell you, keeping it sealed is a nightmare. You're supposed to do it every year, but I think it's been at least three since my husband remembered to buy the spray. 

But um... what did you ask me? Oh, right, thinking about work. No, it doesn't really interrupt me when I'm deep into something else. It's just when my mind is already kind of drifting that I start going over everything that new manager said.
Do you feel anxious most of the time?

Most of the time? No, I wouldn't say most of the time. I mean, I'm perfectly fine when I'm just going about my normal day, like when I'm working in the yard. 

I actually just got my tomato plants in the ground this past weekend. I usually wait until after Mother's Day because you just never know with the frost around here. Last year, we had a freeze warning on May 15th! Can you believe that? I lost half my sweet basil. My neighbor Brenda—the one with the Golden Retriever I was telling you about—she covers her plants with these fancy little plastic cloches she ordered off the internet, but I just use old milk jugs that I cut the bottoms off of. It works exactly the same and it's completely free. You just have to make sure you rinse them out really, really well, otherwise they smell terrible when the sun hits them. My husband forgot to rinse one out a few years ago and the smell in the garage was just... ugh, it smelled like spoiled baby formula for a week. We had to leave the garage doors open with a box fan running just to air it out. 

But, um... sorry, what were you asking? Anxious. Right. No, I'm not walking around feeling anxious all day long. It's really just tied to that manager and having to deal with him, not a constant thing.
Are you avoiding talking to the new manager outside of the scheduled meetings?

Well, I don't really have a choice, do I? I mean, I have to talk to him if there's an issue on the line. But I certainly don't go out of my way to chat with him in the breakroom or anything like that. 

Speaking of the breakroom, the vending machine has been broken for two weeks now. Two weeks! It just eats your quarters and gives you nothing. My coworker, Sarah, lost a whole dollar trying to get a bag of pretzels on Tuesday. She was so mad she actually kicked the machine. I told her she was going to break her toe, wearing those flimsy little flats she always has on. I don't know how she stands on her feet all day in those. I have to wear my orthopedic sneakers with the thick soles, or my lower back is just screaming by three o'clock. I got them at that shoe store out by the mall, the one that always has the "Buy One Get One Half Off" sign in the window. The salesman there, a nice young man named Tyler, said they're the same brand nurses wear. They aren't very stylish, they're just sort of a clunky white leather, but at my age, comfort definitely beats fashion. 

But um... what was the question? Oh, avoiding the manager. Right. No, I don't avoid him if I need to talk to him for work, but I'm definitely not making small talk with him if I don't have to.
Do you ever feel like thoughts about the new manager or work are forcing their way into your mind?

Well, I wouldn't say they force their way in. It's more like I just find myself dwelling on it, you know? Like I'm chewing on the same piece of gristle over and over. 

Speaking of which, we had the toughest pot roast for dinner last night. I don't know what happened, I used the same slow cooker recipe I've used for twenty years. You just put the chuck roast in with a packet of onion soup mix, some carrots, and a little beef broth, and let it go on low for eight hours. Usually, it just falls apart when you touch it with a fork. But this one... I don't know if it was a bad cut of meat or if my slow cooker is finally giving out. I got that slow cooker at a bridal shower back in 1990. It has those little blue geese painted around the outside—very popular back then, everything was country blue and dusty rose. My whole living room used to be decorated in those colors. I even had a dusty rose sofa with a floral pattern that my cat, Mr. Whiskers, absolutely ruined. He used the corners as a scratching post until the stuffing was coming out. We finally had to throw it away when we moved into this house. 

But, um... sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, thoughts forcing their way in. No, they don't really force their way in. I just kind of get stuck thinking about the things he says when I'm already sitting there doing nothing.
Do you feel nervous when interacting with your coworkers?

Nervous with my coworkers? Oh, no, not at all. I've known most of them for years. We all get along just fine. We actually just had a baby shower for one of the girls on the line, Jessica. She's having a little boy. 

We all chipped in and got her one of those fancy strollers, the kind that fold up with one hand? My daughter had one of those when my grandson was born, and let me tell you, they are a lifesaver. When my kids were little, we had those awful umbrella strollers that pinched your fingers every time you tried to close them. I swear I have a scar on my thumb from the one we took to Disney World in '98. We drove all the way down to Florida in a Plymouth Voyager minivan. The air conditioning went out somewhere around Georgia, and the kids were just miserable in the backseat. We had to roll the windows down, and the wind noise was so loud we couldn't even hear the radio. My husband kept trying to sing along to a Beach Boys cassette tape, but he doesn't know the words, he just kind of hums and makes up his own lyrics. It drove me absolutely up the wall. 

But um... what were we talking about? Coworkers. Right. No, I'm not nervous around them. We're all in the same boat, just trying to get through the shift.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with family or friends because of your concerns about the new manager at work?

Well, yes, actually. At home, my husband and I have been arguing a lot more lately. And I just... I haven't been keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I used to. I'm just so drained by the time I get home. 

Usually, we'd watch Jeopardy together after dinner. Alex Trebek, God rest his soul, he was just wonderful, wasn't he? My husband always tries to guess the answers before the contestants, but he's usually wrong. He'll shout out "What is the War of 1812?" for a question about ancient Rome. It used to make me laugh, but lately I just don't have the patience for it. I just want to sit in quiet. We got this new television, one of those flatscreens that takes up half the wall. My son helped us mount it over the fireplace last Thanksgiving. He brought his own drill and everything, but he ended up making three different holes in the drywall before he found the stud. Now there's a big patch job right next to my favorite framed picture of the kids from when they were little. They were wearing these matching red sweaters that my mother knit for them. She was always knitting something, my mother. Blankets, scarves, little booties for babies that hadn't even been born yet. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right, problems because of work. Yeah, it's not just at home, either. My work record has really taken a hit. I've missed some internal deadlines, and I've been pulling back from meetings I'm supposed to be at. I just can't seem to stay on top of things right now.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about work when you're not trying to, and it's disrupting what you're doing?

Well, I wouldn't say it disrupts what I'm doing, exactly. I mean, I don't really find myself thinking about it when I'm busy with other things. Like if I'm out in the garden, I'm just focused on the garden, you know? 

Speaking of the garden, my hydrangeas are just looking terrible this year. I don't know if it's the soil or if we just haven't had enough rain, but the blooms are all small and sort of brownish around the edges. I usually have these big, beautiful blue mopheads. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she always asks what my secret is. I tell her it's coffee grounds! I save all the coffee grounds from my morning pot—I drink Folgers, always have. My husband tried to get me to switch to one of those Keurig machines with the little plastic cups, but I just don't think it tastes the same. Plus, it feels so wasteful, all that plastic going into the landfill. We try to recycle as much as we can. We have this big blue bin that we roll out to the curb every Tuesday morning. The garbage men come so early, though. Sometimes I hear the truck grinding gears at 5:30 in the morning, and it wakes up the dog. Buster is a beagle mix, and once he starts howling, there's no stopping him. He has this high-pitched yodel that just cuts right through the walls. 

But, um... sorry, I lost my train of thought. Work thoughts disrupting things? No, I don't think so. If I'm doing something, I'm usually pretty focused on that.
Do you worry about things other than work, like your health or finances?

No, not really. I mean, my health is fine, and we do okay financially. We've always been pretty careful with our money. My husband has a pension from the phone company, back when it was still Bell Atlantic. He worked there for thirty years, climbing those poles in all kinds of weather. 

I remember one ice storm back in '94, he was out for three days straight restoring power and phone lines. I was stuck at home with the kids, trying to keep the wood stove going. We had this huge pile of oak out back that my brother-in-law chopped for us. He always fancied himself a bit of a lumberjack, my brother-in-law. Wore those red and black plaid flannel shirts even in the middle of summer. He actually moved up to Maine a few years ago, bought a little cabin near Moosehead Lake. We went up to visit him last fall, and the leaves were just spectacular. Bright reds and oranges, like the trees were on fire. We stopped at this little diner on the way up and had the best blueberry pancakes I've ever tasted. The waitress said they picked the blueberries right out back. She had this heavy New England accent, called everyone "dear." It reminded me of my grandmother, she grew up in Boston. She used to make this clam chowder from scratch, the creamy kind, not that red Manhattan stuff. I tried to make it once, but the milk curdled and it was a complete disaster. 

But um... what were you asking? Oh, worrying about health or money. No, no, I don't really worry about those things. It's just the situation at work that's really bothering me.
Do you ever feel like thoughts about the new manager or work are popping into your head unexpectedly, even when you're trying not to think about them?

Well, no, not really popping in out of nowhere. Like I said before, if I'm busy with something, I'm busy. At my job, I'm an inspector, so I'm checking samples and weighing things all day on the line. You really have to keep your eyes peeled for defects. Just last week, I caught a whole batch of bad seals. The rubber was all cracked and brittle. 

It actually reminded me of the weather stripping on my back door at home. My husband keeps saying he's going to replace it before winter, but you know how that goes. The draft in the kitchen gets so bad, I actually had to buy one of those little draft dodgers—you know, the fabric ones that look like a long dachshund dog? I found a cute brown one at a craft fair down at the Methodist church. They always have the best craft fairs in the spring. Mrs. Higgins makes these incredible homemade jams for it. Her strawberry rhubarb is just to die for. I bought three jars last time, but I dropped one right on the driveway and the glass shattered everywhere. It was such a sticky mess, and the ants were all over it by the afternoon. We get those huge black carpenter ants, and they just march right up the concrete in a straight line... 

Um, wait, what were you asking me? Oh, thoughts about the manager popping into my head. No, I don't think so. It doesn't really sneak up on me like that. I just feel stressed when I'm actually dealing with it or thinking about going in.
Do you ever feel like thoughts about the new manager or work are interrupting your other thoughts or activities?

Well, no, not really interrupting. I mean, if I'm doing something, I'm doing it. Like I was saying, if I'm out in the garden or... oh, I didn't tell you about the tomatoes, did I? I'm trying to grow those big heirloom ones this year, the purple Cherokees. They're supposed to be so sweet, but they need a lot of support. I had to go down to the hardware store and buy these heavy-duty wire cages. 

The guy at the hardware store, Mr. Henderson, he's been running that place since I was a little girl. It still smells like sawdust and old metal in there. He has this ancient golden retriever that just sleeps right in the middle of the aisle, and you have to step over him to get to the screws and nails. It's so funny, the dog doesn't even open an eye. My Buster would never do that. If someone walks within ten feet of the house, he's up and barking. We had the mailman try to give him a treat once, but Buster was having none of it. Just barked right at the poor man's hand. 

But um... interrupting my activities? No, I wouldn't say that. The work stuff is just... it's just stressful when I have to face it, you know? But it doesn't really stop me from doing my gardening or anything else.
Do you feel nervous when you're around friends or family, outside of work?

No, I wouldn't say I feel nervous around them. I've always been pretty comfortable with my family and friends. We actually had a barbecue last weekend with my sister and her kids. She brought over this amazing potato salad, the kind with the little bits of hard-boiled egg and paprika sprinkled on top. She uses our mother's recipe, but she adds a dash of pickle juice to the mayonnaise, which gives it this real zing. 

We were sitting out on the patio, and my nephew, he's eight now, he kept trying to catch fireflies in a mason jar. He had holes punched in the lid and everything. It reminded me of when my kids were little, they used to do the exact same thing. We'd stay out until it was pitch black, and the whole yard would be twinkling. They'd always beg to keep the jars in their rooms overnight, but I'd make them let the bugs go so they wouldn't die. 

Oh, and my sister was telling me about her neighbor's cat, this big fluffy orange tabby that keeps sneaking into her garage and sleeping on the hood of her car. She says she has to check every morning before she backs out, just in case he's curled up by the tires... 

But, wait, what did you ask me? Nervous around family? No, no, I feel fine around them. It's really just the work situation that's got me all tied up in knots.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about the new manager or work when you're trying not to?

Well, no, not really. If I want to tune it out, I just put on the television or find something else to do. I've been watching a lot of those cooking competitions lately to unwind. The baking ones are my absolute favorite, though I don't know how they manage to make those giant sculpted cakes without them toppling right over. 

I tried to make a three-tier cake for my daughter's high school graduation years ago, and the bottom layer just completely squished under the weight. It looked exactly like the Leaning Tower of Pisa! We ended up having to just scoop it into bowls and eat it with spoons. It still tasted wonderful, though. I used real vanilla bean in the buttercream frosting. You can always tell the difference when you use the real beans instead of that cheap imitation extract. The imitation one always has this weird, sharp chemical aftertaste to it, kind of like how the breakroom at work smells after the janitors mop the floors. They use this industrial lemon cleaner that just lingers in the air all morning... 

Oh, goodness, I lost my train of thought again. What did you ask me? Thinking about work when I don't want to? No, I don't really do that. If I'm trying not to think about the manager or the stress, I'm usually pretty good at just focusing on my baking shows or whatever else I have going on around the house.
Do you ever feel like you're repeating certain actions or thoughts over and over, even when you don't want to?

Repeating things? Well, I mean, at work I do, obviously. I'm an inspector, so I'm constantly checking the same batches of components all day, weighing them, sorting out the defects. You really get into a rhythm with it. But you mean like... when I don't want to? 

No, not really. I mean, I do have my routines at home. Like my knitting. I'm working on this huge afghan right now for my niece's wedding. It's a chevron pattern, using this gorgeous seafoam green yarn I found on clearance. The cashier at the craft store was telling me they're discontinuing that dye lot, which is just my luck, right? I had to drive to three different stores just to make sure I had enough skeins to finish the border. 

The third store was all the way out in Westlake, and you know how the traffic gets out there by the new outdoor mall... oh, it is just a nightmare. They put in those new roundabouts and nobody knows how to yield. I saw a guy in a red pickup truck just barrel right through the intersection, didn't even tap his brakes. He almost clipped a woman pushing a stroller. It just makes your heart jump right into your throat seeing something like that. I don't understand why people are in such a rush these days. 

Wait, I'm sorry, I got completely off track again. What were we talking about? Repeating thoughts or actions? No, I don't have anything like that. Just my normal day-to-day stuff.
Do you ever feel like thoughts about the new manager or work are entering your mind without you intentionally thinking about them?

Thoughts just entering my mind? No, I wouldn't say they force their way in or anything like that. If I'm thinking about work, it's usually because I'm actively worrying about how I'm going to handle my next shift, you know? 

Like on Tuesday, I was looking at my schedule for the week, and I realized they have me working a double on Friday. I usually don't mind the overtime, it helps pay for my gardening supplies. I just ordered these beautiful heirloom tomato seeds from a catalog. They're called Cherokee Purples, and they grow into these huge, dark, almost bruised-looking tomatoes, but the flavor is just incredible. My grandmother used to grow them back in Ohio. She had this massive garden in her backyard, right next to the old wooden fence that her neighbor painted bright yellow. 

The neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he was a retired postman and he collected vintage license plates. He had them nailed up all over his garage walls. Sometimes he'd let me and my brother come over and look at them. He had one from every single state, even Hawaii and Alaska. The Alaska one had a little bear on it, I think... 

Oh, I'm sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I just start talking and my brain goes right down a rabbit hole. Thoughts entering my mind... no, no, I don't really have that happen. If I'm thinking about the manager, it's because I'm already stressed about having to go in and deal with all the changes. It's not like the thoughts just pop up out of nowhere when I'm trying to relax.

patient.answer:
Well, I haven't really been avoiding the work itself, but... I guess I have been pulling back from some things. Like, I've missed a few internal deadlines lately, which is just not like me at all. My work record has definitely taken a hit. And those meetings I'm supposed to go to? I've been finding excuses to skip them. I just can't sit in that freezing conference room and listen to him talk about "optimizing workflows." 

Speaking of workflows, my husband tried to "optimize" how we load the dishwasher last week. He read some article online about water flow and plate placement, and now he insists all the bowls have to go on the bottom rack. But they don't fit right! The prongs are too close together. I bought this beautiful set of ceramic bowls from a pottery fair in Asheville—we went there for our 25th anniversary, such a lovely trip. The leaves were just starting to turn, and we stayed in this cozy little cabin that smelled like pine... 

But anyway, because of all this stress, we've been arguing a lot more, especially about silly things like the dishwasher. I'm just so drained when I get home that I haven't been keeping up with our usual evening routines. I used to make a nice dinner, maybe do a little gardening out back, but now I just kind of collapse on the sofa. The weeds in my tomato patch are getting completely out of hand. I really need to get out there with the trowel, but I just can't find the energy.

Which reminds me, I actually need to buy a new logbook. The ones they supply us at work have this really thin paper, and my pens always bleed through. I like to use those gel pens, you know? The Pilot G2s. I've been using the blue ones for years, but last week I bought a pack of the purple ones just to spice things up. My granddaughter loves purple. She just turned seven, and her whole birthday party was unicorn themed. Purple balloons, purple frosting on the cupcakes... oh, those cupcakes were so sweet they made my teeth ache. I think my daughter got them from that big supermarket chain, not a real bakery. You can always tell the difference in the buttercream. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, the meetings. Yeah, no, I don't feel like I *can't* stop thinking about them if I really tried, I just... I don't know, I just end up dwelling on them when I'm tired.

I spent three hours trying to scrub the stains out with club soda and baking soda. My neighbor Brenda swears by that combination for everything, even her dog's messes. We even switched him to that expensive grain-free food, the salmon pate—he absolutely refuses to eat the chicken one, he'll just sit by his bowl and glare at you until you open a different can. My husband and I remodeled our kitchen back in 2008, right before the market crashed, and we kept the walls up. I like having the kitchen separate. That way, if I have guests over and the sink is full of dirty pots, nobody has to look at it while we're eating. We did put in granite countertops, though. "Giallo Ornamental," they called it. It has these lovely little flecks of gold and brown. But let me tell you, keeping it sealed is a nightmare. You're supposed to do it every year, but I think it's been at least three since my husband remembered to buy the spray. 

But um... what did you ask me? Oh, right, thinking about work. No, it doesn't really interrupt me when I'm deep into something else. It's just when my mind is already kind of drifting that I start going over everything that new manager said.

It works exactly the same and it's completely free. You just have to make sure you rinse them out really, really well, otherwise they smell terrible when the sun hits them. My husband forgot to rinse one out a few years ago and the smell in the garage was just... ugh, it smelled like spoiled baby formula for a week. We had to leave the garage doors open with a box fan running just to air it out. 

But, um... sorry, what were you asking? Anxious. Right. No, I'm not walking around feeling anxious all day long. It's really just tied to that manager and having to deal with him, not a constant thing.

I have to wear my orthopedic sneakers with the thick soles, or my lower back is just screaming by three o'clock. I got them at that shoe store out by the mall, the one that always has the "Buy One Get One Half Off" sign in the window. The salesman there, a nice young man named Tyler, said they're the same brand nurses wear. They aren't very stylish, they're just sort of a clunky white leather, but at my age, comfort definitely beats fashion. 

But um... what was the question? Oh, avoiding the manager. Right. No, I don't avoid him if I need to talk to him for work, but I'm definitely not making small talk with him if I don't have to.

My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she always asks what my secret is. I tell her it's coffee grounds! I save all the coffee grounds from my morning pot—I drink Folgers, always have. My husband tried to get me to switch to one of those Keurig machines with the little plastic cups, but I just don't think it tastes the same. Plus, it feels so wasteful, all that plastic going into the landfill. We try to recycle as much as we can. We have this big blue bin that we roll out to the curb every Tuesday morning. The garbage men come so early, though. Sometimes I hear the truck grinding gears at 5:30 in the morning, and it wakes up the dog. Buster is a beagle mix, and once he starts howling, there's no stopping him. He has this high-pitched yodel that just cuts right through the walls. 

But, um... sorry, I lost my train of thought. Work thoughts disrupting things? No, I don't think so. If I'm doing something, I'm usually pretty focused on that.

No, not really. I mean, my health is fine, and we do okay financially. We've always been pretty careful with our money. My husband has a pension from the phone company, back when it was still Bell Atlantic. He worked there for thirty years, climbing those poles in all kinds of weather. 

I remember one ice storm back in '94, he was out for three days straight restoring power and phone lines. I was stuck at home with the kids, trying to keep the wood stove going. We had this huge pile of oak out back that my brother-in-law chopped for us. He always fancied himself a bit of a lumberjack, my brother-in-law. Wore those red and black plaid flannel shirts even in the middle of summer. He actually moved up to Maine a few years ago, bought a little cabin near Moosehead Lake. We went up to visit him last fall, and the leaves were just spectacular. Bright reds and oranges, like the trees were on fire. We stopped at this little diner on the way up and had the best blueberry pancakes I've ever tasted. The waitress said they picked the blueberries right out back. She had this heavy New England accent, called everyone "dear." It reminded me of my grandmother, she grew up in Boston. She used to make this clam chowder from scratch, the creamy kind, not that red Manhattan stuff. I tried to make it once, but the milk curdled and it was a complete disaster. 

But um... what were you asking? Oh, worrying about health or money. No, no, I don't really worry about those things. It's just the situation at work that's really bothering me.

I found a cute brown one at a craft fair down at the Methodist church. They always have the best craft fairs in the spring. Mrs. Higgins makes these incredible homemade jams for it. Her strawberry rhubarb is just to die for. I bought three jars last time, but I dropped one right on the driveway and the glass shattered everywhere. It was such a sticky mess, and the ants were all over it by the afternoon. We get those huge black carpenter ants, and they just march right up the concrete in a straight line... 

Um, wait, what were you asking me? Oh, thoughts about the manager popping into my head. No, I don't think so. It doesn't really sneak up on me like that. I just feel stressed when I'm actually dealing with it or thinking about going in.

Sometimes he'd let me and my brother come over and look at them. He had one from every single state, even Hawaii and Alaska. The Alaska one had a little bear on it, I think... 

Oh, I'm sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I just start talking and my brain goes right down a rabbit hole. Thoughts entering my mind... no, no, I don't really have that happen. If I'm thinking about the manager, it's because I'm already stressed about having to go in and deal with all the changes. It's not like the thoughts just pop up out of nowhere when I'm trying to relax.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of anxiety and stress related to the new manager at work, avoidance of certain tasks or situations, and impact on relationships and daily life are consistent with an adjustment disorder. However, the lack of persistent and intrusive thoughts or compulsions to perform specific rituals, and the absence of a clear traumatic stressor, make F41.1 (Anxiety disorder due to known physiological condition) and F48.0 (Other neurotic disorders) less likely. F43.0 (Acute stress disorder) is also considered but the duration and nature of symptoms do not fully align.
